sub_criteria.name: baseline recall ceiling
sub_criteria.text: Reports or measures the recall/precision ceiling of single-query database search (BM25, embedding search, or a search API) as a comparison point.

sub_criteria.name: agentic mechanism gain
sub_criteria.text: Attributes a measured gain to a specific agentic move — query reformulation, citation-graph traversal, or iterative crawling — rather than to the system as an undifferentiated whole.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval/reranking method
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates a retrieval or reranking technique underlying an agentic literature-search system (dense retrieval, learned reranker, hybrid search).

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Explains how an evaluation set for literature-search agents was built — query source, relevance labeling, corpus coverage, contamination controls.

sub_criteria.name: gain replication failure
sub_criteria.text: Shows a reported agentic gain shrinking, disappearing, or failing to generalize under a different benchmark, metric, or independent replication.

items.abstract_600: Language models have shown promising performance on the task of translating natural language questions into SQL queries (Text-to-SQL). items.abstract_600: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) aims to create transparency in modern AI models by offering explanations of the models to human users. There are many ways in which researchers have attempted to evaluate the quality of these XAI models, such as user studies or proposed objective metrics like "fidelity". items.abstract_600: Reproductions in NLP/ML indicate worryingly low levels of reproducibility, but their results are hard to interpret, compare, and learn from, because reported in qualitative terms with varying, often unstated, criteria. items.abstract_600: Large Language Models (LLMs) have drawn a lot of attention due to their strong performance on a wide range of natural language tasks, since the release of ChatGPT in November 2022. items.abstract_600: Machine learning has the potential to provide tremendous value to life sciences by providing models that aid in the discovery of new molecules and reduce the time for new products to come to market. items.abstract_600: The rapid rise of Large Language Models (LLMs)-based intelligent agents underscores the need for robust, scalable evaluation frameworks. items.title: Estimating Soil Parameters From Hyperspectral Images: A benchmark dataset and the outcome of the HYPERVIEW challenge
items.abstract_600: Enhancing agricultural methods through the utilization of Earth observation and artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a significant concern. The ability to quantify soil parameters on a large scale can play a pivotal role in optimizing the fertilization process. While techniques for noninvasive estimation of soil parameters from hyperspectral images (HSIs) exist, their validation typically occurs across different datasets and employs varying validation protocols. This diversity renders them inherently challenging (or even impossible) to compare objectively.

items.abstract_600: Reproducibility serves as a fundamental aspect of biomedical research, guaranteeing that findings are reliable, precise, and relevant to clinical applications.
